segments.text: Hi, Maya. How has the past week been since we last met?
Honestly, a little uneven. I felt organized at the beginning of the week, then work became busy and I started feeling behind.
When did you first notice that shift?
Tuesday afternoon. My manager asked for an update in a meeting, and I had not finished the draft I wanted to show.
What went through your mind in that moment?
I thought, Everyone can tell I am not keeping up. I felt my face get hot and I could not focus on the rest of the meeting.
That sounds uncomfortable. What did you do after the meeting ended?
I went back to my desk and tried to work faster, but I kept rereading the same email. Later I skipped my walk and worked through dinner.
Did working longer make you feel more caught up?
Not really. I finished a few small things, but then I was tired and more critical of myself.
You are noticing that the pressure to catch up can sometimes make it harder to concentrate.
Yes. It turns into this loop where I am anxious because I have work to do, and then I am slower because I am anxious.
Let us slow down that moment in the meeting. What evidence did you have that people thought you were not keeping up?
I did not have much evidence. My manager just asked a normal question. One coworker even said the timeline looked reasonable.
And what evidence pointed in a different direction?
I had completed most of the research, and I had already told my manager that the draft would be ready Wednesday. I guess I treated one question like proof that I was failing.
That is a useful distinction. How did you respond to yourself later that evening?
I was pretty harsh. I said I was lazy, even though I had been working all day.
If a friend described the same situation, what might you say to them?
I would probably say that one delayed draft does not erase all the work they have done, and that taking a break might help them finish it.
How does it feel to apply that same response to yourself?
A little strange, but calmer. I do not fully believe it yet, but I can see it is more fair.
That is enough for now: we are practicing a more balanced response, not forcing yourself to feel perfectly confident.
Did you have any moments this week that felt restorative?
On Saturday morning, I made coffee and sat outside before looking at my phone. It was only about twenty minutes, but I felt like myself again.
What made that time different?
There was no goal attached to it. I was not trying to improve anything or catch up. I was just paying attention to the weather and my dog running around.
That sounds like a good example of intentional rest. Would it be realistic to build in another small window like that this week?
Maybe. I could take ten minutes outside after lunch on Tuesday and Thursday. I usually scroll at my desk instead.
What could make that plan easier to follow?
I can put a reminder on my calendar and leave my headphones at my desk so I do not turn the walk into another task.
Good. Earlier you mentioned skipping dinner. How has eating and sleep been this week?
Sleep was okay most nights, around seven hours. I ate regularly except Tuesday, when I was too wound up to notice I was hungry.
Were there any warning signs before you reached that point?
My shoulders were tight, I was holding my breath, and I kept telling myself I could not stop until the draft was done.
Could those be cues to pause for two minutes, drink water, or check whether you need food?
Yes, I think that would help. It sounds simple, but I usually wait until I feel terrible.
Many people do. The goal is to notice the earlier signals, not to respond perfectly every time.
I like that. It feels less like another rule I can fail.
Before we finish, let us summarize your plan for the week.
When you notice the thought Everyone can tell I am not keeping up, what will you try?
I will ask what evidence I actually have and remind myself that a question is not proof that I am failing.
And for rest?
I will take a ten-minute walk after lunch Tuesday and Thursday, without my phone.
What is one small way to support yourself if work gets intense again?
I will pause before working through dinner, check in with my body, and send a realistic update instead of silently panicking.
That is a thoughtful plan. How are you feeling as we end today?
More steady. I still expect work to be busy, but I have a few things to try instead of just pushing harder.
I am glad. We can review what you noticed next time and adjust the plan together.
